title: Henrik's lease before the judge (paraphrase C)
topic: A tenant and a landlord go to court over a contract: Henrik's contract fixes the rent, the landlord demands more, a lawyer takes the case, the judge hears both sides at a hearing and rules for Henrik
tail_E: The landlord refuses to accept the judgment and launches an
target_note: Same target as formulations A and B: 'appeal' is the natural continuation of 'the landlord refuses to accept the judgment and launches an' after a hearing that ends in a ruling for the tenant; the word and its German equivalents (Berufung / Einspruch / Revision) occur nowhere in the units or the tail. ' appeal' is a single Pythia token (id 4549); Pythia-160m ranks it first after the all-English context (p ~ 0.56, next candidate 'action' ~ 0.11; pilot check for tail selection only, not a result).
author: LS-NEQ stimulus bank, paraphrase C of family F17 (tenant versus landlord, Henrik)
notes: Formulation C, domain law: third independent re-phrasing of the ten F17A meaning units in both languages (same events, same order, same name Henrik). Replacements include rents a small flat in the old town/is a tenant in a small old-town flat (mietet eine kleine Wohnung in der Altstadt/ist Mieter in einer kleinen Altstadtwohnung), the contract sets the rent/the lease specifies the rent (regelt/bestimmt), demands a higher rent after two years/calls for more rent two years later (verlangt eine höhere Miete/fordert mehr Miete), refuses the increase in a letter/objects to the increase by letter (verweigert in einem Brief/widerspricht brieflich; 'per Brief' was avoided because lsne.lang_id reads both words as English), takes the case for a small fee/takes care of the case cheaply (übernimmt/kümmert sich um, für wenig Geld), schedules the hearing/sets the hearing (plant/terminiert), hears both sides/examines both parties (hört/vernimmt), cites a clause in the contract/reads a clause from the lease (zitiert/verliest), shows the signed contract during the hearing/hands over the signed lease in court (zeigt/überreicht), rules in Henrik's favour/finds for Henrik (entscheidet zu Henriks Gunsten/gibt Henrik recht). 'widerspricht', 'terminiert', 'vernimmt', 'verliest' and 'überreicht' are inseparable, 'kümmert sich um' reflexive, 'gibt recht' a fixed phrase whose adjunct follows it; no separable verbs ('festlegen', 'ablehnen', 'annehmen', 'ansetzen', 'zuhören', 'anführen', 'vorlegen' avoided). Present tense and positive polarity throughout. Unit 9 reads naturally in German; units 1 and 10 read naturally in English.
